directive: Render a thin, low-mass breadcrumb strip (Home › Blog › Article title) fixed below the navbar. Minimum tap target 44px. Server-rendered to match BreadcrumbList JSON-LD schema.org markup. Single function: one-tap escape back to /blog without competing with the H1 for first fixation.
hypothesis: A low-mass breadcrumb that anchors location and provides a one-tap exit to /blog without competing with the H1 for first fixation reduces disoriented-bounce rate among readers who land cold from search.
arbitration_note: Confidence is low because breadcrumbs on editorial luxury sites have weak empirical evidence; server-rendering is non-negotiable for the JSON-LD SEO signal regardless.

directive: Stack: small all-caps tag/eyebrow (suppress if no category) → Playfair H1 (dominant mass, the LCP element, server-rendered) → dek (1-2 lines) → byline + meta line. Zero competing CTA in the header viewport. H1 is the single header-viewport pop-out.
hypothesis: A clean primacy header that commits the reader (no competing CTA) raises scroll-depth into the body, the precondition for any concierge action.
arbitration_note: CTA is explicitly excluded from the header; its absence is the decision. The H1 must be the only heavy element in the first viewport.

directive: Render within the meta line: 'By Camille Roux · Travel Editor' with monogram/avatar linked to /about. Replace any generic 'Admin User' attribution. Graceful fallback: 'Natlaupa Editorial · Curated by our travel team' + credible one-liner when author data is generic. Server-rendered for E-E-A-T signal.
hypothesis: A named human author with a linked profile and travel-editor title reduces bounce by establishing first-impression credibility over generic author attribution.
arbitration_note: Author data may be generic in CMS; fallback copy must be pre-defined. Server-rendering is mandatory so Google can index the E-E-A-T signal.

directive: Remove the view count display entirely from the meta row. Keep date and reading-time (suppress reading-time if under 3 min). Do not fabricate or inflate counts.
hypothesis: Removing the view count prevents a low honest number from acting as a credibility liability on a luxury surface, which would otherwise elevate first-impression bounce.
arbitration_note: Ethics floor — no fabricated or inflated counts. Honest removal is the only compliant option. Luxury positioning demands omission over a low signal.

directive: Reserve an exact 16:9 aspect-ratio box for the cover at all times. When no cover exists, fill the identical box with a typographic/gradient title-plate fallback (deep gradient + fine gold rule); never a gray void. Never restate the H1 inside the cover. Zero CLS between cover and no-cover states.
hypothesis: A reserved cover box with a typographic fallback eliminates CLS between cover and no-cover states, and the non-H1 fallback avoids redundancy that would dilute the primacy header's visual weight.
arbitration_note: The box must be identical in both variants (cover and fallback) so next/image with fill + priority can satisfy CWV. H1 must not appear inside the cover (redundancy).

directive: Prose column max-width ~68ch (640-720px). Inter 18-19px, leading 1.65, warm off-white (--text-100/300) on deep-800 meeting WCAG AA ≥4.5:1. Left-aligned, generous paragraph spacing. Real H2/H3 subheads in Playfair. Server-rendered as static HTML (H1 + full body in initial HTML — SEO non-negotiable). Sanitize injected <style>/inline color/font from CMS so brand prose owns all styling.
hypothesis: Prose at 68ch max-width, 18-19px, leading 1.65, on deep-800 sustains reading without fatigue and increases scroll depth into the body where the concierge action is available.
arbitration_note: Server-rendering of full body is a hard SEO constraint. CMS output must be sanitized to strip injected styles before rendering into the brand prose column.

directive: Apply block-group opacity fade (250-400ms ease, one group per logical content cluster — never per-paragraph). Must be fully readable with JavaScript disabled. Entrance animation only; no looping or attention-stealing motion.
hypothesis: Block-group opacity fade adds entrance motion that guides eye flow through the body without disrupting reading or creating accessibility failures for JS-disabled users.
arbitration_note: Per-paragraph animation is banned (too fragmented). JS-disabled must render all content visible immediately. Motion must have a job (flow guidance) not be decorative.

directive: Render a quiet sticky aside TOC in the desktop margin (outside the prose column). Suppress entirely on mobile. Conditional: only show for articles with ≥ 6 H2 headings or > 1500 words. Desktop only: does not enter the mobile bottom zone.
hypothesis: A quiet sticky TOC in the desktop margin speeds navigation on long reads without diverting thumb-zone space from the mobile sticky CTA, increasing scroll depth on long-form articles.
arbitration_note: vs sticky CTA on mobile bottom — CTA wins unconditionally; TOC is desktop-margin-only. Confidence is low because TOC usage data on editorial luxury sites is sparse.

directive: At ~50-60% through the body, insert an in-flow editorial aside with a gold hairline left border, Playfair invitation line, and a quiet 'Speak to a concierge' text link. Weight comes from isolation and whitespace, not from a colored box or banner. Copy is help-framed: 'Planning a stay like this? Our concierge can check availability and rates for you — no obligation.'
hypothesis: An in-flow editorial aside weighted through isolation (not a saturated banner) at the point of maximum interest escapes banner blindness and triggers a concierge action from readers who would ignore a conventional ad-box.
arbitration_note: Biology (in-flow, no ad-box) vs physics (heavy mass) → heavy-via-isolation, not via a saturated banner. Both constraints satisfied by the gold hairline + Playfair + whitespace pattern.

directive: After the body and before the end CTA: monogram/photo + name + one-line role + 1-2 line credible bio citing first-hand travel experience + link to /about. Low mass — must not out-mass the end CTA. For generic author data: collapse to one-line attribution, hide bio text block.
hypothesis: A named author bio with first-hand travel credentials placed after the body but before the end CTA reinforces E-E-A-T and warms the reader for the concierge action without out-massing the end CTA.
arbitration_note: Author bio must be visually subordinate to the end CTA. Mass hierarchy: end CTA > author bio. Fallback for generic author must not introduce fake credentials.

directive: One isolated block on deep-700 with maximal whitespace, Playfair invitation heading, ONE primary CTA button (≥48px, gold accent — its only permitted use of gold on the page), reassurance microcopy ('Human concierge, 24/7 · reply on WhatsApp or email · no account or payment to ask a question'), and ONE restrained org-trust line ('Natlaupa — a registered French travel house, RCS Nanterre'). No newsletter signup, no share buttons inside this block.
hypothesis: Concentrating the page's only end pop-out and peak-end emphasis on an isolated end CTA maximises concierge_action_rate vs scattering equal-weight CTAs across the page.
arbitration_note: Secondary goals (newsletter, share, related articles) are demoted outside this block. The trust line is one high-fluency unit and must not out-mass the primary button. Gold is its one permitted accent — no other element on the page uses solid gold.

directive: Place related articles after the end CTA, not before it. Maximum 3 cards. Weight-demoted (smaller than the end CTA). Reuse list grid's typographic fallback pattern and reserved cover boxes. Render only if ≥ 2 genuinely relevant articles exist — no padding articles, no lone card.
hypothesis: Related articles placed after the end CTA protect the primary concierge action while offering a low-friction next step for readers not yet ready to enquire, sustaining site engagement.
arbitration_note: Engagement goal (related early and prominent) is explicitly subordinated to the conversion goal (end CTA first). Related section is a safety net for non-converting readers, not a primary element.

directive: Mobile: docked bottom bar (56-64px, thumb arc, single large target) rendered in static HTML; entrance opacity+translateY 250-400ms ease after header scrolls past. Container padding-bottom = bar height so it never covers last line / author bio / footer. Yields (translateY 100%) when end CTA band is fully in view (IntersectionObserver threshold 0.8). Desktop: docked in margin outside the ~680px prose column. Coordinate with site-level floating WhatsApp button — exactly ONE concierge prompt visible at a time on the detail page.
hypothesis: A persistent docked concierge CTA at the mobile thumb arc ensures the primary action is always reachable without competing with prose reading; yielding when the end CTA enters view prevents double-CTA confusion.
arbitration_note: vs TOC mobile-bottom → CTA wins unconditionally. vs no-load-animation → defer entrance until header passes (avoids distraction on load). vs end CTA → yields when end-CTA band is fully visible (no double CTA). vs WhatsApp float → coordinate: this bar replaces or suppresses the float on the detail page. Ethics floor: no nagging, no re-appearing after yield.
